regime: Federal Law No. 282-FZ on Digital Currencies and Digital Rights (2026)
description_en: The State Duma adopts the law in second and third readings.

regime: Federal Law No. 282-FZ on Digital Currencies and Digital Rights (2026)
description_en: Signed and officially published as Federal Law No. 282-FZ of 4 August 2026 'On Digital Currencies and Digital Rights'.

regime: Federal Law No. 282-FZ on Digital Currencies and Digital Rights (2026)
description_en: The law comes into effect.

regime: Federal Law No. 282-FZ on Digital Currencies and Digital Rights (2026)
description_en: The Bank of Russia enters the first five digital depositories and the first four organisations conducting digital currency exchange (crypto exchanges) in its new registers, under the law's transitional provisions. From entry they must follow the rules for executing and recording digital-currency transactions, and they must bring their activities into compliance with the law before 1 September 2027. As of 30 October 2026 the registers list 8 digital depositories and 23 crypto exchange organisations, with no exclusions.

regime: Federal Law No. 282-FZ on Digital Currencies and Digital Rights (2026)
description_en: The Bank of Russia enters the first self-regulatory organisation (SRO) for digital depositories and organisations conducting digital currency exchange (crypto exchanges) in its unified register of financial-market SROs; the SRO is NAUFOR, which already became the first SRO for information system operators on 8 October 2026. Under Federal Law No. 282-FZ, digital depositories and crypto exchange organisations entered in the Bank of Russia's registers must join an SRO within 90 days (the Bank of Russia release does not state the exact start date of this period).

regime: Federal Law No. 282-FZ on Digital Currencies and Digital Rights (2026)
description_en: The Bank of Russia officially publishes Indication No. 7441-U of 11 September 2026 (MinJust registration No. 88991 of 30 October 2026). It lists Bitcoin (BTC) and Ethereum Ether (ETH) as digital currencies that an organiser of trade may admit to public circulation on organised trading, and USD Tether (USDT) as a foreign digital instrument on the same basis. Non-qualified investors may buy through a broker, manager or crypto exchange organisation up to ₽300,000 a year per intermediary after testing; qualified investors face no amount limit but must also take the test.

regime: Federal Law No. 282-FZ on Digital Currencies and Digital Rights (2026)
description_en: The Bank of Russia officially publishes Indication No. 7438-U of 8 September 2026 (MinJust registration No. 89019 of 3 November 2026), amending Regulation No. 437-P on organised trading. Exchanges may open organised trading in digital currencies and digital rights from 22 November 2026 once the Bank of Russia has approved their trading rules. Organisers must register trading participants, keep registers of orders and trades, calculate price indicators (current, weighted-average, market and closing prices) and report trading information to the Bank of Russia in the same way as for other assets.

regime: Federal Law No. 282-FZ on Digital Currencies and Digital Rights (2026)
description_en: Indication No. 7441-U enters into force (10 days after official publication on 6 November 2026). From this date organisers of trade may admit Bitcoin, Ethereum Ether and USD Tether to public circulation under the Indication.

regime: Federal Law No. 282-FZ on Digital Currencies and Digital Rights (2026)
description_en: Indication No. 7438-U enters into force. From this date exchanges may open organised trading in digital currencies and digital rights once the Bank of Russia has approved their trading rules.

regime: Federal Law No. 282-FZ on Digital Currencies and Digital Rights (2026)
description_en: Moscow Exchange (MOEX) plans to launch Russia's first organised digital-currency market from 1 December 2026, initially with BTC, ETH and USDT in pilot trades as participants connect (planned; MOEX announcement of 2 November 2026).

regime: Federal Law No. 282-FZ on Digital Currencies and Digital Rights (2026)
description_en: From this date residents (other than organisers of digital-currency circulation) may carry out digital-currency transactions only through or with organisers of circulation, such as licensed brokers and registered crypto exchange organisations; direct person-to-person (P2P) deals are permitted only until this date (Art. 30(1), Bank of Russia FAQ). The Bank of Russia's July release describes the transition period for market participants to obtain licences and comply as running through 1 July 2027.

regime: Federal Law No. 282-FZ on Digital Currencies and Digital Rights (2026)
description_en: Credit institutions, brokers and firms acting as authorised organisations or liquidity providers in the experimental legal regime may file for entry in the crypto exchange register under the simplified procedure until ('до') 1 September 2027; the Bank of Russia decides no later than one working day after receiving the documents. Organisations already admitted under the transitional provisions must bring their activities into compliance before 1 September 2027.

regime: Act on the Protection of Virtual Asset Users
description_en: The Virtual Asset User Protection Act takes effect: VASPs must safeguard user deposits and assets and monitor and report abnormal trading, under FSC supervision and sanctions.

regime: Act on the Protection of Virtual Asset Users
description_en: The FSC announces a full security inspection of about 580 financial firms, including VASPs: registered external-contact systems by 30 November 2026, and unregistered systems plus internal controls by 31 December 2026. A November guideline is planned so VASPs report incidents to the FSS and FSI as well as KISA, and a Digital Financial Safety Act draft is planned for Q1 2027.

regime: Act on the Protection of Virtual Asset Users
description_en: The FSC issues emergency security-incident response guidelines for VASPs, says it will issue a no-action letter allowing preventive deposit and withdrawal blocks when a hack is suspected (terms and date not yet published), and says it will revise the specialised virtual-asset exchange security inspection standard by the end of 2026. The release states that 5 of 28 VASPs — the five won-market exchanges — are members of the Financial Security Institute.

regime: Act on the Protection of Virtual Asset Users
description_en: Deadline for the full check of external-contact systems listed on financial firms' IT asset registers, including VASPs.

regime: Act on the Protection of Virtual Asset Users
description_en: Deadline for the full check of unregistered systems and of CEO/CISO internal-control arrangements across about 580 financial firms, including VASPs.

regulator: Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) Thailand · Ministry of Finance
regime: Emergency Decree on Digital Asset Businesses B.E. 2561 (2018)
description_en: The Emergency Decree on Digital Asset Businesses comes into force. Exchanges, brokers and dealers need a licence from the Minister of Finance on the SEC's recommendation.

regulator: Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) Thailand · Ministry of Finance
regime: Emergency Decree on Digital Asset Businesses B.E. 2561 (2018)
description_en: Deadline (90 days) for existing operators to apply to the SEC if they wanted to keep operating.

regulator: Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) Thailand · Ministry of Finance
regime: Emergency Decree on Digital Asset Businesses B.E. 2561 (2018)
description_en: SEC Thailand files a criminal complaint against BG Limited (Bitget) for operating a digital asset exchange without a licence and asks the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society to block access to Bitget from 5 December 2026.

regulator: Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) Thailand · Ministry of Finance
regime: Emergency Decree on Digital Asset Businesses B.E. 2561 (2018)
description_en: Scheduled start of the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society access block for Bitget platforms, as notified by the SEC on 5 November 2026.
The Senate passes the Virtual Asset Service Providers Bill, 2026, after the House of Assembly passed it on 6 October 2026.

The President assents to the Virtual Asset Service Providers Act, 2026 (Act 2026-25), published in the Official Gazette (Part A No. 122). It commences the same day. The Financial Services Commission administers the Act; providing virtual asset services in, or to persons in, Barbados requires an FSC licence or certificate of registration.

Deadline for providers already serving Barbados before commencement to inform the FSC and apply for a licence or certificate of registration: within 3 months of commencement (s. 27; date is a VASP Tracker calculation).

regulator: OCC · Federal Reserve · FDIC · NCUA · state regulators · Treasury
description_en: The GENIUS Act is enacted (Public Law 119-27).

regulator: OCC · Federal Reserve · FDIC · NCUA · state regulators · Treasury
description_en: Treasury publishes an interim final rule on the review of state certifications. The notice states that the Act's effective date is expected to be 18 January 2027.

regulator: OCC · Federal Reserve · FDIC · NCUA · state regulators · Treasury
description_en: The OCC announces a final rule implementing the GENIUS Act for permitted and foreign payment stablecoin issuers under its jurisdiction and certain custody activities by OCC-supervised entities. Bank Secrecy Act, AML and OFAC rules will follow in a separate rulemaking. The OCC states that the rule and the Act take effect on 18 January 2027.

regulator: OCC · Federal Reserve · FDIC · NCUA · state regulators · Treasury
description_en: Expected effective date. Section 20 makes the Act effective on the earlier of 18 months after enactment or 120 days after the primary federal regulators issue final implementing rules. Treasury gives 18 January 2027 as the expected date.
The FCA application window opens at 9:00. Firms apply for authorisation, or for a variation of permission, through FCA Connect.
The application window closes at 23:59. Existing firms that apply within the window can keep operating while their application is assessed, if no decision has been made before the regime starts.
Full commencement: cryptoasset activities become FCA-regulated activities and require authorisation.
Parliament passes the Digital Assets Framework Act.
Royal Assent.

Comments are due on ASIC CP 392 (released 15 October 2026): draft guidance for DAPs and TCPs, draft asset-holding and transactional and settlement standards, and draft financial requirements. ASIC plans to publish the final instruments and guidance in March 2027.

The Act commences: s. 2 sets the day after the end of the 12 months beginning on Royal Assent, which the Act's commencement table gives as 8 April 2027. Digital asset platforms (DAPs) and tokenised custody platforms (TCPs) come under the financial services licensing regime, and licence applications open. ASIC's earlier roadmap page gives 9 April 2027; its CP 392 gives 8 April 2027.

Existing operators of a platform that is a DAP or TCP on 8 April 2027 must apply for an AFS licence or a licence variation by this date. ASIC says they can keep operating while it assesses the application.

regime: Act amending the FIEA and the Payment Services Act (Act No. 64 of 2026)
description_en: The government submits the bill to the Diet.

regime: Act amending the FIEA and the Payment Services Act (Act No. 64 of 2026)
description_en: The Diet enacts the Act. Crypto-asset trading regulation moves from the Payment Services Act to the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act.

regime: Act amending the FIEA and the Payment Services Act (Act No. 64 of 2026)
description_en: First provisions take effect 20 days after promulgation: higher penalties for unregistered business and new criminal-investigation powers for the SESC.

regime: Act amending the FIEA and the Payment Services Act (Act No. 64 of 2026)
description_en: Latest date for the main provisions. The Act takes effect on 'a date set by Cabinet Order within one year of promulgation' (Supplementary Provisions, art. 1). Promulgation was 23 July 2026, derived from the FSA's 20-day count, so the latest date is 22 July 2027 by our calculation. The Cabinet Order date has not been announced.
The Stablecoin Act receives Royal Assent, enacted by section 600 of the 2026 budget implementation statute (S.C. 2026, c. 3).

regulator: Bank of Ghana (BoG) · Securities and Exchange Commission
description_en: Parliament passes the Virtual Asset Service Providers Act, 2025 (Act 1154), Under the Act, the Bank of Ghana works with the SEC and the Financial Intelligence Centre to register and license VASPs.
Stablecoin issuer regime takes effect: issuing fiat-referenced stablecoins becomes a regulated activity that needs an HKMA licence.
FSTB and SFC conclude consultations on licensing virtual-asset dealers and custodians and plan to introduce a bill into the Legislative Council in 2026.
HKMA grants the first two stablecoin issuer licences, to Anchorpoint Financial Limited and The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited.

regime: Virtual Assets Service Providers Act (passed Oct 2026) · VASP (Licensing) Regulations, 2026 (not yet in force)
description_en: The House of Representatives approves the Virtual Assets Service Providers Bill.

regime: Virtual Assets Service Providers Act (passed Oct 2026) · VASP (Licensing) Regulations, 2026 (not yet in force)
description_en: The Senate has approved the Virtual Assets Service Providers Act (reported 12 Oct 2026). The Act introduces mandatory licensing, supervision and enforcement powers aligned with FATF Recommendation 15, with the Financial Services Commission as the regulatory authority.

regime: Virtual Assets Service Providers Act (passed Oct 2026) · VASP (Licensing) Regulations, 2026 (not yet in force)
description_en: The Senate affirms the Virtual Asset Service Providers (Licensing) Regulations, 2026, which set the FSC licence application requirements (ownership and control, management, safeguarding of customer assets, AML controls, technology risk, financial capacity) and ongoing duties such as annual declarations and seven-year record keeping.

regime: MiCA applies directly · national act on the crypto-asset market not in force
description_en: The Sejm passes the first act on the crypto-asset market, a government bill (print 1424): 230 for, 196 against. It is sent to the President on 12 November 2025.

regime: MiCA applies directly · national act on the crypto-asset market not in force
description_en: The President vetoed the first act (motion dated 1 December 2025). The Sejm fails to override the veto: 243 for, 192 against, short of the 3/5 majority required.

regime: MiCA applies directly · national act on the crypto-asset market not in force
description_en: The Sejm passes a second act on the crypto-asset market, again a government bill (print 2064): 241 for, 183 against, 1 abstention. It is sent to the President on 26 January 2026.

regime: MiCA applies directly · national act on the crypto-asset market not in force
description_en: The President vetoed the second act (motion dated 12 February 2026). The Sejm fails to override the veto: 243 for, 191 against, 3 abstentions, short of the 3/5 majority required.

regime: MiCA applies directly · national act on the crypto-asset market not in force
description_en: The Sejm passes a third act on the crypto-asset market (print 2529, considered jointly with prints 2363, 2528 and 2530): 241 for, 200 against. It would designate the KNF as supervisor. The President vetoes it on 11 June 2026.

regime: MiCA applies directly · national act on the crypto-asset market not in force
description_en: IAS Katowice: an entry in the Polish virtual-currency register is not a MiCA authorisation and gives no right to operate after 1 July 2026.

regime: MiCA applies directly · national act on the crypto-asset market not in force
description_en: The MiCA transitional period (Art. 143(3)) ends. The 6 months Poland notified to ESMA were never written into law, so the MiCA end date applies directly. IAS Katowice, the authority for the virtual-currency register: 'z dniem 1 lipca 2026 r. kończy się okres przejściowy' (the transitional period ends on 1 July 2026). Because no implementing act is in force, no Polish authority, including the KNF, has been designated as competent authority, so CASP authorisations cannot be obtained in Poland.

regime: MiCA applies directly · national act on the crypto-asset market not in force
description_en: The Sejm fails to override the veto on the third act: 241 for, 198 against, 3 abstentions, short of the 3/5 majority required.

regime: FinIA amendment: payment instrument institutions and crypto institutions (draft)
description_en: The consultation on the draft creating two new licence types closes: payment instrument institutions, which could issue stablecoins, and crypto institutions for custody and trading.
The Legislative Yuan passes the Virtual Asset Service Act on third reading.
The Act is promulgated. It is not yet in force; the Executive Yuan sets the effective date (Art. 56).

The FSC announces draft implementing rules for consultation (40 days from Gazette publication): 8 VASP regulations, with minimum paid-in capital of NT$50m (exchange, transfer, underwriting), NT$100m (trading platform, custody) or NT$200m (lending), and stablecoin issuance rules requiring NT$300m for non-bank issuers. Drafts only; they are to take effect with the Act.

regime: Law No. 7518 (amending Capital Markets Law 6362) · Communiqué III-35/B.1
description_en: Law No. 7518 is published in the Official Gazette, bringing crypto-asset service providers under SPK licensing.

regime: Law No. 7518 (amending Capital Markets Law 6362) · Communiqué III-35/B.1
description_en: SPK decision 18/617 extends two deadlines: providers on the 'operating list' to obtain authorisation, and platforms to sign and file custody agreements. The new deadline will be set after SPK-authorised custodians begin providing custody to platforms widely.

regime: Law No. 7518 (amending Capital Markets Law 6362) · Communiqué III-35/B.1
description_en: The Financial Stability Board publishes a peer review of Türkiye. It recommends a dedicated stablecoin-issuer regime and a defined CASP licensing schedule; the review is not binding and creates no new legal obligations. The review records that the CMB extended authorisation deadlines at the end of March 2026 (already on this page as SPK decision 18/617 of 26 March 2026); that as of late June 2026 six banks had preliminary BRSA approval and the CMB had found three banks suitable for crypto custody; and that MASAK applies crypto-to-crypto stablecoin transfer limits of USD 3,000 a day and USD 50,000 a month.

regulator: National Securities and Stock Market Commission (NSSMC) · National Bank of Ukraine
regime: Draft law on virtual assets (passed first reading, Sept 2025)
description_en: The NSSMC reports that the virtual assets bill, which passed first reading in September 2025, makes the NSSMC the main crypto-market regulator and the National Bank of Ukraine the supervisor of e-money tokens. The chair expects the new law to apply from 2027.
Law 14,478 sets the legal framework for virtual-asset service providers.
BCB Resolutions 519, 520 and 521 published (authorisation, operating rules, FX).
Resolution 520 takes effect.
Deadline for providers already operating to file for BCB authorisation.

Art. 91 of Res. BCB 520 (wording from Res. BCB 589) takes effect: banks, payment institutions and other BCB-authorised institutions may no longer carry out or enable operations with virtual-asset providers that are not authorised by the BCB, except in forms the rule expressly allows. The amended text no longer mentions firms 'in the authorisation process'. The BCB has not clarified whether art. 88 §6 continuity for timely filers counts as a form 'expressamente autorizada' under art. 91.

BCB publishes on bcb.gov.br the list of companies that declared they provide virtual-asset services and applied for authorisation under art. 88 of Res. BCB 520: 120 applications, 119 under examination and 1 rejected (73 intermediary, 46 broker, 1 custodian requested). Inclusion does not mean authorisation. A second list names 24 BCB-authorised institutions eligible to provide virtual-asset services under art. 22 of Res. 520.

regulator: Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) Nigeria · Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN)
regime: Investments and Securities Act, 2025 · SEC ARIP · CBN Non-Security Virtual Asset Regulations
description_en: The Investments and Securities Act, 2025 commences. It gives the SEC power to register, regulate and supervise virtual asset service providers and digital asset operators.

regulator: Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) Nigeria · Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN)
regime: Investments and Securities Act, 2025 · SEC ARIP · CBN Non-Security Virtual Asset Regulations
description_en: CBN circular PSP/DIR/PUB/CIR/001/004 issues the Regulations for the Operations of Non-Security Virtual Assets in Nigeria, effective 5 November 2026. They license stablecoins, Deposit Money Tokens and related non-security VASP services under the CBN's payments mandate and do not displace the SEC's mandate over security virtual assets. Class 1 issuer paid-up capital is ₦10 billion; Class 2 is ₦15 billion; other non-security services are ₦1 billion (ss. 15–16). Section 2.2 prohibits algorithmic stablecoins and other listed Prohibited Tokens. Existing operators must apply within 180 calendar days, register within 30 days and begin supervisory reporting within 60 days (s. 54; calculated deadlines 4 May 2027, 5 December 2026 and 4 January 2027).

regulator: Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) · Capital Markets Authority (CMA)
regime: Virtual Asset Service Providers Act, 2025 (Act No. 20 of 2025)
description_en: The VASP Act, 2025 receives presidential assent (published in the Kenya Gazette on 21 October 2025).

regulator: Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) · Capital Markets Authority (CMA)
regime: Virtual Asset Service Providers Act, 2025 (Act No. 20 of 2025)
description_en: The Act commences. CBK and CMA become the licensing authorities; carrying on virtual-asset business in or from Kenya without a licence is an offence (s. 8).

regulator: Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) · Capital Markets Authority (CMA)
regime: Virtual Asset Service Providers Act, 2025 (Act No. 20 of 2025)
description_en: CBK and CMA public notice: licensing will start once the National Treasury issues Regulations; no VASP has been licensed under the Act.

regulator: Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) · Capital Markets Authority (CMA)
regime: Virtual Asset Service Providers Act, 2025 (Act No. 20 of 2025)
description_en: Public participation on the draft VASP Regulations, 2026 (published 17 March 2026 with a Regulatory Impact Statement) closes; the National Treasury held forums in eleven towns from 30 March. The draft set higher capital floors than the final text, e.g. KSh 150 million for an exchange and KSh 500 million for a stablecoin issuer.

regulator: Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) · Capital Markets Authority (CMA)
regime: Virtual Asset Service Providers Act, 2025 (Act No. 20 of 2025)
description_en: The Virtual Asset Service Providers Regulations, 2026 (Legal Notice 134 of 2026) are published in the Kenya Gazette and commence the same day. They set out licence applications, capital, governance, consumer-protection, stablecoin and tokenisation rules; the regulator must decide a complete application within 30 days (reg. 6(4)).

regulator: Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) · Capital Markets Authority (CMA)
regime: Virtual Asset Service Providers Act, 2025 (Act No. 20 of 2025)
description_en: Section 47 gives anyone already providing virtual-asset services one year from commencement to comply with the Act. One year from 4 November 2025 is 4 November 2026 (VASP Tracker calculation); that window has now closed, and an existing provider without a licence is exposed to the s. 8(3) offence.

regulator: Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) · Capital Markets Authority (CMA)
regime: Virtual Asset Service Providers Act, 2025 (Act No. 20 of 2025)
description_en: A joint CBK and CMA public notice confirms that the VASP Regulations, 2026 (Legal Notice 134, Kenya Gazette Supplement No. 185, 22 July 2026) operationalise the VASP Act. Anyone providing or intending to provide virtual asset services must apply for a licence; both regulators will publish lists of licensed VASPs.

regime: NAPP licensing regulation for crypto-asset service providers (reg. no. 3380, 2022)
description_en: The NAPP regulation on licensing crypto-asset service providers (exchanges, depositories, stores, mining pools) is registered by the Ministry of Justice (reg. no. 3380).

regime: NAPP licensing regulation for crypto-asset service providers (reg. no. 3380, 2022)
description_en: NAPP's register shows crypto-exchange licence CE #0007 issued to COINPAY on 12 October 2026, the most recent crypto-exchange licence listed.
The new CBUAE law takes effect.

End of the one-year period for persons subject to the law to bring their positions into line (Art. 184). One year from the law taking effect on 16 September 2025 is 16 September 2026 (VASP Tracker calculation). The CBUAE Board may extend it; we found no published general extension (checked 21 Oct 2026).

regime: Virtual Assets Act, 2026 · Virtual Asset Services Regulations, 2026
description_en: PVARA treats persons operating on or before 5 March 2026 as 'transitional persons' under section 70 of the Virtual Assets Act, 2026.

regime: Virtual Assets Act, 2026 · Virtual Asset Services Regulations, 2026
description_en: The Virtual Asset Services Regulations, 2026 and the Activity Specific Regulations, 2026 are notified in the Gazette and take effect. Licensing runs in steps: a No-Objection Certificate (NOC, valid 3 months), then incorporation in Pakistan, then a licence application decided within 90 days.

regime: Virtual Assets Act, 2026 · Virtual Asset Services Regulations, 2026
description_en: Deadline for transitional persons to submit an NOC application, or cease operations (s. 70). A complete application lets them continue while it is pending, subject to PVARA's interim directives.
Titles III and IV apply: asset-referenced tokens and e-money tokens (stablecoins).
MiCA applies in full, including CASP authorisation (Art. 63). National transitional periods of up to 18 months begin (Art. 143(3)).
ESMA statement: after 1 July 2026, any entity providing crypto-asset services to EU clients without a MiCA licence is in breach of EU law.
ESMA public statement: unauthorised CASPs must immediately stop onboarding EU clients and wind down in an orderly way.
The last national transitional periods end. Art. 143(3) caps all of them at 1 July 2026.
The European Banking Authority classifies USDC, issued by Circle Internet Financial Europe SAS, as the first significant e-money token under MiCA.

Dual supervision of USDC by the EBA and the ACPR begins. The EBA takes over direct supervision of own funds, the reserve of assets, liquidity requirements and recovery and redemption plans; the ACPR remains responsible for governance, qualifying holdings, fit-and-proper assessments, outsourcing and conflicts of interest.

regulator: Financial Supervision Commission (FSC) / Bulgarian National Bank
description_en: MiCA applies in full, including CASP authorisation. Financial Supervision Commission (FSC) / Bulgarian National Bank is the competent authority for crypto-asset service providers on ESMA's Article 93 list.

regulator: Financial Supervision Commission (FSC) / Bulgarian National Bank
description_en: ESMA's list notes that entities on the Bulgarian VASP register between 30 December 2024 and 8 July 2025 (when the Bulgarian implementing act entered into force) had to apply for MiCA authorisation before 8 October 2025.

regulator: Financial Supervision Commission (FSC) / Bulgarian National Bank
description_en: Bulgaria's transitional period ends. The FSC: 'На 1 юли 2026 г. приключва преходният период' (the transitional period ends on 1 July 2026).
MiCA applies in full, including CASP authorisation. Cyprus Securities and Exchange Commission (CySEC) is the competent authority for crypto-asset service providers on ESMA's Article 93 list.
Cyprus's transitional period ends. CySEC: existing providers 'may continue to do so until 1 July 2026'.
MiCA applies in full, including CASP authorisation. Česká národní banka (CNB) is the competent authority for crypto-asset service providers on ESMA's Article 93 list.
ESMA's list notes that, to benefit from the Czech transitional period, applicants had to apply before 31 July 2025.
Czechia's transitional period ends. The CNB: '1. července 2026 skončí přechodné období' (the transitional period ends on 1 July 2026).
MiCA applies in full, including CASP authorisation. Finanstilsynet (DK FSA) is the competent authority for crypto-asset service providers on ESMA's Article 93 list.
ESMA's list notes that, to benefit from the Danish transitional period, applicants had to apply before 30 December 2024.

End of Denmark's transitional period. The Danish FSA describes it only as 'i en periode på op til 18 måneder' (up to 18 months) without a day; 1 July 2026 is the Art. 143(3) MiCA cap (VASP Tracker derivation).
MiCA applies in full, including CASP authorisation. Finantsinspektsioon (EFSA) is the competent authority for crypto-asset service providers on ESMA's Article 93 list.
Estonia's transitional period ends. The EFSA: 'Kuni käesoleva aasta 1. juulini võivad …' (existing providers may operate until 1 July of this year).
MiCA applies in full, including CASP authorisation. CNMV (CASPs) · Banco de España (ARTs/EMTs) is the competent authority for crypto-asset service providers on ESMA's Article 93 list.

Spain's transitional period ends. The CNMV: 'El periodo transitorio en España finalizará el 1 de julio de 2026'. Since then only CNMV-authorised providers, or providers authorised in another EU state, may operate in Spain.
MiCA applies in full, including CASP authorisation. AMF / ACPR is the competent authority for crypto-asset service providers on ESMA's Article 93 list.
France's transitional period for registered PSANs ends. The AMF: the transitional period 'prend fin le 1er juillet 2026'.
MiCA applies in full, including CASP authorisation. HANFA (CASPs) · Croatian National Bank (ARTs/EMTs) is the competent authority for crypto-asset service providers on ESMA's Article 93 list.
Croatia's transitional period ends. HANFA: 'On 1 July 2026, the transitional period under Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 …' ends; from then a HANFA licence or registration is mandatory.
MiCA applies in full, including CASP authorisation. CSSF is the competent authority for crypto-asset service providers on ESMA's Article 93 list.
Luxembourg's transitional period for registered VASPs ends. The CSSF: 'On 1 July 2026, an important transition period … ended'.
MiCA applies in full, including CASP authorisation. Banco de Portugal (authorisation) / CMVM (supervision) is the competent authority for crypto-asset service providers on ESMA's Article 93 list.

Portugal's transitional period ends. Law 69/2025, art. 30(1): providers registered with the Banco de Portugal may continue 'até 1 de julho de 2026' or until MiCA authorisation is granted or refused, whichever comes first.
MiCA applies in full, including CASP authorisation. Not yet designated (ESMA list: 'TBA') is the competent authority for crypto-asset service providers on ESMA's Article 93 list.

The transitional period ends in Romania. No Romanian implementing law sets its own date, so the Art. 143(3) MiCA end date applies directly; the ASF notice relays ESMA: the period ends 'la 1 iulie 2026'.
The EEA MiCA Implementation Act (EWR-MiCA-DG) enters into force; MiCA applies in Liechtenstein.
End of the transitional period for TT service providers registered under the TVTG whose business now falls under MiCA.

regime: MiCA · Act No. 101/2025 on markets in crypto-assets
description_en: Act No. 101/2025, which implements MiCA in Iceland, takes effect.

regime: MiCA · Act No. 101/2025 on markets in crypto-assets
description_en: From this date, VASPs registered under the AML Act may no longer provide services without a licence from the Central Bank.
MiCA applies in full, including CASP authorisation. FSMA / National Bank of Belgium (NBB) is the competent authority for crypto-asset service providers on ESMA's Article 93 list.
Belgium's transitional period ends: the FSMA says providers relying on it could continue 'jusqu'au 30 juin 2026 au plus tard' (until 30 June 2026 at the latest).

regulator: Hellenic Capital Market Commission (HCMC) / Bank of Greece
description_en: MiCA applies in full, including CASP authorisation. Hellenic Capital Market Commission (HCMC) / Bank of Greece is the competent authority for crypto-asset service providers on ESMA's Article 93 list.

regulator: Hellenic Capital Market Commission (HCMC) / Bank of Greece
description_en: Greece's transitional period ends. Law 5193/2025 art. 125(1), as amended by Law 5259/2025 art. 204, lets registered providers continue 'έως την 30ή Ιουνίου 2026' (until 30 June 2026). Read from an unofficial consolidation; the HCMC's own notice relays ESMA's 1 July 2026.

regulator: Hellenic Capital Market Commission (HCMC) / Bank of Greece
description_en: The Hellenic Parliament passes a Ministry of National Economy and Finance bill on the tax treatment and supervision of crypto-assets. It taxes capital gains on crypto-asset transfers at a special 10% rate and gives the HCMC supervisory and technical measures against unlicensed crypto-asset services and other illegal offers made through websites and apps. The final text has not yet been published in the Government Gazette (FEK).
MiCA applies in full, including CASP authorisation. CONSOB / Banca d'Italia is the competent authority for crypto-asset service providers on ESMA's Article 93 list.
ESMA's list notes that entities in the Italian VASP register (or their group entities) had to file a MiCA application by 30 December 2025 to benefit from the transitional period.

Italy's transitional period ends. Art. 45 of Legislative Decree 129/2024, as amended by Decree-Law 95/2025, replaces '30 dicembre 2025' with '30 giugno 2026': providers may continue 'comunque non oltre il 30 giugno 2026' (in any case not after 30 June 2026).
MiCA applies in full, including CASP authorisation. Malta Financial Services Authority (MFSA) is the competent authority for crypto-asset service providers on ESMA's Article 93 list.
Malta's transitional period ends. The MFSA: the transitional provisions 'as implemented in Article 66 of the Virtual Financial Assets Act, Cap. 590, expire on 30 June 2026'.
The Act on crypto-assets (kryptoeiendelsloven), which implements MiCA in Norway, enters into force.
Finanstilsynet extends the transitional period in § 19 of the Act from 30 December 2025 to 30 June 2026 for providers registered under the AML Act.

End of the extended transitional period under § 19 of the Act on crypto-assets, as extended by Finanstilsynet 'fra 30. desember 2025 til 30. juni 2026'. Providers without MiCA authorisation are expected to wind down in an orderly way. ESMA's list (19 May 2026) still shows 12 months.

regulator: National Agency for Virtual Assets and Blockchain Technologies under the President (NAVA)
regime: Law of the Kyrgyz Republic on Virtual Assets · NAVA licences (trading operators, exchange operators, miners)
description_en: Presidential Decree No. 112 sets the minimum charter capital of a virtual-asset trading operator (crypto exchange).

regulator: National Agency for Virtual Assets and Blockchain Technologies under the President (NAVA)
regime: Law of the Kyrgyz Republic on Virtual Assets · NAVA licences (trading operators, exchange operators, miners)
description_en: Presidential Decree No. 186 on the authorised body for virtual-asset policy and regulation, with the Regulation on NAVA; NAVA licenses the virtual-asset market and keeps the registries.

regime: Crypto assets as financial products · FAIS Act No. 37 of 2002
description_en: The FSCA starts licensing crypto asset service providers (CASPs) under the FAIS Act.

regime: Crypto assets as financial products · FAIS Act No. 37 of 2002
description_en: By the end of its 2025/26 financial year the FSCA had received 533 CASP licence applications: 310 approved, 17 declined, 124 withdrawn. It had opened 81 investigations into suspected unlicensed CASP businesses.
MiCA applies in full. The KMAG provides the German supervisory framework, with BaFin as competent authority.

Germany's transitional period ends: under KMAG § 50(2) no. 3, the deemed authorisation of existing providers expires 'spätestens mit Ablauf des 31. Dezember 2025' (at the latest at the end of 31 December 2025). ESMA's list shows 12 months.
MiCA applies in full, including CASP authorisation. Finanzmarktaufsicht (FMA) is the competent authority for crypto-asset service providers on ESMA's Article 93 list.
Austria's transitional period ends: under § 23 MiCA-VVG, providers could continue their services 'bis zum 31. Dezember 2025' (ESMA's list: 12 months).
MiCA applies in full, including CASP authorisation. Bank of Lithuania is the competent authority for crypto-asset service providers on ESMA's Article 93 list.
Lithuania's transitional period ends. The Bank of Lithuania: 'a transitional period will remain in effect until 31 December 2025' (extended by the Seimas from the original 1 June 2025).
MiCA applies in full, including CASP authorisation. Central Bank of Ireland is the competent authority for crypto-asset service providers on ESMA's Article 93 list.

Ireland's transitional period ends. S.I. No. 607/2024, reg. 20: existing providers 'may continue to do so until 30 December 2025'. (The Central Bank's MiCA page describes it as 12 months ending on 29 December 2025.)
MiCA applies in full, including CASP authorisation. Národná banka Slovenska (NBS) is the competent authority for crypto-asset service providers on ESMA's Article 93 list.
Slovakia's transitional period ends. The NBS: 'Dňa 30.12.2025 sa na Slovensku oficiálne skončilo 12 mesačné prechodné obdobie'.
MiCA applies in full, including CASP authorisation. Finansinspektionen (FI) is the competent authority for crypto-asset service providers on ESMA's Article 93 list.

Sweden's statutory transitional date. Transitional provision 4 of Act 2024:1159 lets existing firms continue 'till och med den 30 september 2025'. Firms that applied before 1 October 2025 could continue until their application was finally decided, within the MiCA cap; FI says that period ran out at the end of June 2026.
Resolution 05/2025/NQ-CP comes into force, opening a five-year pilot of a licensed crypto-asset market.

The Ministry of Finance publishes the licensing procedures (Decision 96/QD-BTC) and the State Securities Commission starts accepting applications for a licence to operate a crypto-asset trading market. Under the pilot, an applicant needs at least VND 10,000 billion of paid-up charter capital.
End of the five-year pilot period (VASP Tracker calculation).

regime: BSP Circular No. 1108 (2021) · VASP Certificate of Authority
description_en: BSP Circular No. 1108 sets the guidelines for virtual asset service providers (VASPs), covering exchange, transfer and safekeeping of virtual assets; VASPs need a BSP Certificate of Authority.

regime: BSP Circular No. 1108 (2021) · VASP Certificate of Authority
description_en: The BSP closes the regular application window for new VASP licences for three years. Existing BSP-supervised financial institutions may still apply.

regime: BSP Circular No. 1108 (2021) · VASP Certificate of Authority
description_en: The BSP continues the moratorium on new VASP licences, citing consumer protection and cybercrime, subject to reassessment.

regime: BSP Circular No. 1108 (2021) · VASP Certificate of Authority
description_en: BSP coin and token listing guidelines for VASPs (Memorandum M-2026-023); privacy coins may not be listed or supported.
MiCA applies in full, including CASP authorisation. Agencija za trg vrednostnih papirjev (ATVP) is the competent authority for crypto-asset service providers on ESMA's Article 93 list.

Slovenia's transitional period ends. ZIUTK art. 21(1): existing providers continue 'do 1. julija 2025' (until 1 July 2025) or until authorisation is granted or refused. The ATVP: 'S 1. julijem 2025 se je … zaključilo prehodno obdobje'.

regime: Financial Services and Markets Act 2022, Part 9 (DTSPs)
description_en: The DTSP regime takes effect. Singapore-based firms providing digital-token services only to customers outside Singapore need a licence, and MAS said it would generally not grant one.
MiCA applies in full, including CASP authorisation. Finanssivalvonta (FIN-FSA) is the competent authority for crypto-asset service providers on ESMA's Article 93 list.
Finland's transitional period ends. FIN-FSA: 'siirtymäaika päättyi 30.6.2025' (the transitional period ended on 30 June 2025).
MiCA applies in full, including CASP authorisation. Magyar Nemzeti Bank (MNB) is the competent authority for crypto-asset service providers on ESMA's Article 93 list.

End of Hungary's transitional period. Act VII of 2024 § 16 requires existing providers to comply 'legkésőbb 2025. július 1-jétől' (from 1 July 2025 at the latest), so the last transitional day is 30 June 2025 (VASP Tracker derivation from the statutory date).
MiCA applies in full, including CASP authorisation. Latvijas Banka is the competent authority for crypto-asset service providers on ESMA's Article 93 list.

Latvia's transitional period ends. The Crypto-Asset Services Law lets existing providers continue 'līdz 2025. gada 30. jūnijam' (until 30 June 2025); applicants that filed by then may continue until their application is decided.
MiCA applies in full, including CASP authorisation. AFM (CASPs) / De Nederlandsche Bank is the competent authority for crypto-asset service providers on ESMA's Article 93 list.
The Dutch transitional period ends. The AFM: existing providers 'per 30 juni 2025 een vergunning of notificatie moeten hebben' (must hold a licence or notification as of 30 June 2025).
RG 1058/2025 is published in the Boletín Oficial, setting registration, cybersecurity, custody, AML and disclosure obligations for PSAVs.
RG 1058/2025 enters into force 45 days after publication (art. 9); 45 days from 14 March 2025 is 28 April 2025 (VASP Tracker calculation). New PSAV registrations were suspended until then (art. 4).
Deadline for registered PSAVs that are natural persons to file the required information; otherwise their registration is cancelled.
Deadline for registered locally incorporated companies.
Deadline for foreign companies (branch registration or local subsidiary).
Full-compliance date: all remaining RG 1058 requirements become enforceable for PSAVs already registered.
VASP registration with CIMA begins under the Virtual Asset (Service Providers) Act (phase one).
Phase two: amendments commence and the licensing regime starts for virtual asset custodians and virtual asset trading platforms.

regime: POJK 27/2024 on trading of digital financial assets including crypto assets (Law 4/2023 P2SK)
description_en: POJK 27/2024 is promulgated. Law 4/2023 (P2SK) required supervision of digital financial assets to move from Bappebti to the OJK within 24 months, by 12 January 2025.

regime: POJK 27/2024 on trading of digital financial assets including crypto assets (Law 4/2023 P2SK)
description_en: POJK 27/2024 takes effect and the OJK becomes regulator and supervisor of crypto-asset trading.

regime: Virtual Asset Service Providers Act, 2024 (Act 12 of 2024)
description_en: The VASP Act, 2024 is published in the Official Gazette.

regime: Virtual Asset Service Providers Act, 2024 (Act 12 of 2024)
description_en: Deadline for providers operating on 1 September 2024 to apply for a licence; from 1 January 2025, those that had not applied must stop operating.

regime: Digital Assets and Registered Exchanges Act, 2024 (DARE 2024)
description_en: The Digital Assets and Registered Exchanges Act, 2024 comes into force, replacing DARE 2020 with a broader registration regime for digital asset businesses, including stablecoin and staking rules.

regime: Digital Assets and Registered Exchanges Act, 2024 (DARE 2024)
description_en: Latest SCB list of registered DARE firms (as at 30 April 2026).

regime: AIFC Rules on Digital Asset Activities (AIFC Rules FR00062 of 2023)
description_en: The AIFC Rules on Digital Asset Activities, approved on 10 September 2023, commence and govern digital asset trading facilities and other digital asset firms in the Astana International Financial Centre.

regime: PMLA 2002 · VDA service providers as reporting entities (S.O. 1072(E))
description_en: The Finance Ministry's notification S.O. 1072(E) brings virtual digital asset service providers (VDA SPs) under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act as reporting entities. Exchange, transfer, custody and issuer-related services must register with FIU-IND.

regime: PMLA 2002 · VDA service providers as reporting entities (S.O. 1072(E))
description_en: FIU-IND issues show-cause notices to nine offshore VDA SPs operating without registration and asks for their URLs to be blocked. The obligation is activity-based and does not depend on physical presence in India; 31 VDA SPs had registered by then.
The Virtual Assets Service Providers Act, 2022 comes into force; VASPs must register with the FSC.
Deadline for persons already carrying on VASP business to apply for registration.
The Virtual Assets Act, 2023 becomes operational; the Bank of Namibia is the regulatory authority for VASPs and initial token offerings.

regime: Lending, Credit and Finance (Bailiwick of Guernsey) Law, 2022 · VASP licensing
description_en: The Lending, Credit and Finance Law, 2022 comes into force. Virtual asset service providers need a GFSC licence.

regime: NBG rule on registration and supervision of VASPs (2023)
description_en: The NBG approves the rule on registration and regulation of virtual asset service providers.

regime: NBG rule on registration and supervision of VASPs (2023)
description_en: The registration rule comes into force; VASPs must register with the NBG.

regime: Proceeds of Crime (Jersey) Law 1999, Schedule 2 · VASP registration
description_en: The Proceeds of Crime (Amendment No. 6) (Jersey) Order 2022 widens the regime from virtual currency exchanges, registered since 2016, to all virtual asset service providers, in line with FATF standards. Businesses operating before 30 January 2023 must register with the JFSC to continue.

regime: Proceeds of Crime (Jersey) Law 1999, Schedule 2 · VASP registration
description_en: End of the transition period for existing businesses to register as VASPs with the JFSC.

regulator: Comisión Nacional de Activos Digitales (CNAD) · Banco Central de Reserva (BCR)
regime: Ley de Emisión de Activos Digitales (2023) · Ley Bitcoin
description_en: The Legislative Assembly adopts the Digital Assets Issuance Law (Decree 643). It creates the CNAD, which registers digital asset service providers (PSAD).

regulator: Comisión Nacional de Activos Digitales (CNAD) · Banco Central de Reserva (BCR)
regime: Ley de Emisión de Activos Digitales (2023) · Ley Bitcoin
description_en: In force eight days after publication in the Diario Oficial of 24 January 2023 (Art. 47; VASP Tracker calculation).

regime: Virtual Asset and Initial Token Offering Services Act 2021 (VAITOS)
description_en: The VAITOS Act 2021 is proclaimed and comes into force. Existing VASPs and ITO issuers must apply within 3 months; custodians had 18 months.

regulator: National Bank of Serbia (NBS) · Securities Commission
regime: Law on Digital Assets (Official Gazette RS 153/2020)
description_en: The Law on Digital Assets enters into force (Art. 146).

regulator: National Bank of Serbia (NBS) · Securities Commission
regime: Law on Digital Assets (Official Gazette RS 153/2020)
description_en: The law begins to apply; digital asset service providers need NBS (virtual currencies) or Securities Commission (digital tokens) authorisation.

regime: Financial Services (DLT Providers and VAA Providers) Regulations 2020
description_en: The Financial Services (DLT Providers and VAA Providers) Regulations 2020 are made under the Financial Services Act 2019. Firms using DLT to store or transmit value for others need a GFSC DLT licence. Last amended March 2026.

Banxico Circular 4/2019 is published: banks and ITFs may use virtual assets only for internal operations, with prior Banxico authorisation; they may not offer exchange, transfer or custody services to clients.
The CBB issues final rules for crypto-asset services and crypto-asset exchanges: licensing, governance, capital, AML/CFT, conduct, reporting and cyber security.
The CBB grants Fasset Financial Services W.L.L. a Crypto Asset Service Provider – Category 3 licence.
The CBB introduces a framework for licensing stablecoin issuers: single-currency stablecoins backed by BHD, USD or another fiat currency acceptable to the CBB.

regime: Digital Currency and Digital Token Prescription Order 2019 · Recognized Markets (DAX) Guidelines
description_en: The Capital Markets and Services (Prescription of Securities) (Digital Currency and Digital Token) Order 2019 comes into force; the SC that offering and trading digital assets will require SC authorisation and compliance with securities laws.

regime: Digital Currency and Digital Token Prescription Order 2019 · Recognized Markets (DAX) Guidelines
description_en: Latest update (20 July 2026) of the SC list of registered digital asset exchanges.
The Digital Asset Business Act 2018 receives assent.
The Digital Asset Business Act 2018 becomes operative (Commencement Day Notice, BR 97/2018). From then on, digital asset business in or from Bermuda needs a BMA licence.
With the Act in effect, the BMA publishes its licence application requirements: Class F (full), Class M (modified) licences cover exchanges, custodians, payment providers and dealers.
